Implemented in commit d8708e3, pushed to origin/main.

**What shipped.** A `MarkdownCodeBlock` renderer (new file) mounted through the existing `MarkdownContent` component map as `pre`, so every fenced block in a message, tool card or reasoning card now shows a header with the fence's language tag and a small Copy button. New files: `MarkdownCodeBlock.tsx`, `clipboard.ts`, `markdownCode.css`.

**Exact source, not the rendered form.** The copied text is read back recursively from the block's own `code` element props rather than from the DOM, so wrapping, highlighting or a future highlighter cannot change the payload. A test asserts the clipboard receives `"const answer = 42;\n"` verbatim for a fenced block.

**One clipboard implementation.** `clipboard.writeClipboard` prefers the async Clipboard API and falls back to the deprecated `execCommand('copy')` where it is missing, resolving false rather than throwing. `clipboard.useCopyFeedback` gives the one-second confirmation and clears its timer on unmount. `RawJsonView` (the Run details Raw tab) was moved onto the same helper, so the two inline `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` call sites became one.

**Acceptance criteria.** (1) every fenced block gets the control, including one with no language tag; (2) exact source copied, no trailing content added by the control; (3) one-second "Copied" confirmation, and a refused write reports nothing rather than claiming success — both tested, including the `execCommand` path; (4) nothing is copied automatically and non-code content renders unchanged; (5) keyboard reachable with a tooltip, an accessible label that reflects the copied state, and a focus ring; (6) one shared helper, used here and by the Raw tab.

**Judgement calls.** The header sits outside the scrolling `<pre>` so it stays visible on long blocks, and its own selector is deliberately more specific than `.bubble-markdown pre` so the parent's bubble styles cannot detach it. The confirmation swaps the button's accessible label as well as its text, so a screen reader hears the outcome.

**Verification.** `npx vitest run src/chat src/workbench` 57 files / 446 tests passed (four new); `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vite build` succeeded; the three new files are Prettier-clean. `MarkdownContent.test.tsx` is already non-conforming at HEAD, so I formatted only the block I appended and confirmed Prettier no longer reports anything inside it, rather than reformatting the file.

## What

Add a small copy control at the top of every fenced code block rendered in a Chat message, matching what DSH does and what the operator finds handy there. Aworkit today renders code blocks with no way to copy them.

## Why

In the first DSH vs Aworkit benchmark the operator could copy a code or raw-text block straight from the message in DSH, and cannot in Aworkit. The only copy affordance Aworkit has anywhere is the "Copy JSON" button in the Run Details Raw tab (`desktop/src/chat/RawJsonView.tsx:23-27`), which is a different surface and is not reachable from a message.

## Where

* Renderer: `desktop/src/chat/MarkdownContent.tsx` (58 lines). It renders `ReactMarkdown` with `components={{ a: MarkdownLink }}` and an allow-list that already includes `code` and `pre`, so the change is a `pre` (or `code`) component override that wraps the block in a header plus the existing `<pre>` — no new dependency and no raw HTML (the module deliberately keeps raw HTML disabled).
* Styles: the message code-block rules live in `desktop/src/styles.css` (`.bubble-markdown pre` around line 921 and `code, pre` around line 114), so the header styling belongs beside them unless a small dedicated stylesheet is preferred.
* Pattern to follow from DSH: `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx` puts the copy button in the block header, `use-copy-feedback.ts` keeps a one-second "copied" confirmation, and `clipboard.ts` falls back to `execCommand('copy')` when the async Clipboard API is missing (insecure contexts, jsdom).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every fenced code block in a message shows a small copy control in its header, including blocks without a language tag and blocks inside a tool or reasoning card.
2. Clicking it copies the block's exact text — the original source, not the rendered or highlighted form — with no trailing content added.
3. A short confirmation follows a successful write (DSH uses a one-second label swap), and a refused or unavailable clipboard is reported rather than silently ignored.
4. Nothing is copied automatically, and the control never appears when there is no code block.
5. The control is keyboard reachable with a tooltip and an accessible label, and stays usable at the narrow chat widths the bubble supports.
6. The copy behaviour lives in one place: extract the write plus feedback into a small shared helper or component and use it here and in `RawJsonView.tsx` instead of leaving two inline `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` calls.

## Tests

Extend `desktop/src/chat/MarkdownContent.test.tsx` to cover: the control renders for a fenced block, the copied payload is the exact block source, the confirmation appears and clears, and an unavailable clipboard does not throw. A jsdom test needs the `execCommand` fallback path, which is why the helper must not call `navigator.clipboard` unguarded.

data.title: Add a copy control to message code blocks
